# Downloads the JSON Swagger document
cd `dirname $0`
set -e
stage=dev
region=us-east-1 # must match serverless.yml:provider.region
apiId=`bash -c "aws apigateway get-rest-apis --output=json --region=$region | /usr/bin/env node ./extract-rest-api-id.js $stage"`
fileType=json
outputFileName=serverless-aws-documentation-example-$STAGE.$fileType
printf "Downloading Swagger definition to ./$outputFileName
  API ID: $apiId
   Stage: $stage
  Accept: $fileType\n\n"

aws apigateway get-export \
  --rest-api-id=$apiId \
  --stage-name=$stage \
  --export-type=swagger \
  --accept=application/$fileType \
  --region=$region \
  $outputFileName

printf "\n$(tput setaf 2)Done, your swagger document is: ./$outputFileName$(tput sgr0)\nGo to http://editor.swagger.io/ and paste the contents of your swagger document to see it in Swagger UI"

It then downloads the Swagger JSON export of the API to a local file named with a variable stage (though $STAGE is undefined, likely a bug). The script performs network operations via AWS CLI to fetch API metadata and writes the output to a local file. The hardcoded region and stage parameters, combined with the use of AWS CLI and Node.js, enable automated retrieval of potentially sensitive API definitions, facilitating reconnaissance or further exploitation.

The only minor issue is a likely bug with an undefined variable ($STAGE), which does not imply maliciousness.
